A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlphaRec research despite the changed title and organization. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments, linear-mapping evaluations, ablations, zero-shot results, and user-intention analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model-size, prompt-noise, and LLMRank comparison results.

M1.justification: Equation (1) changes the stated user initialization: v1 averages MLP-transformed historical item embeddings, whereas v2 applies the MLP to their average language embedding. These procedures are not equivalent for a nonlinear MLP. Graph propagation and InfoNCE remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the equation revision reflects an implementation change or a documentation correction.

E1.justification: v2 adds Steam as a zero-shot evaluation population in Appendix D.2.3 and evaluates noisy item-title inputs in Section 3.2. The original six datasets remain; Industrial becoming Industrial & Scientific is a renaming, not added coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated LLMRank comparator in Appendix D.2.3, Table 8. The comparator sets in the retained general recommendation, full-ranking zero-shot, and intention-capture comparisons remain unchanged. LLMRank's underlying work was already cited in v1, but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: Added evaluations use Llama2 sizes of 7B, 13B, and 70B, titles with 5–10 random letters appended, and a separate LLMRank protocol with one positive plus 19 negative candidates and NDCG@1/5/10/20. These supplement the retained protocols; the documented 4:3:3 splits, filtering, and main training hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends the investigation of encoded collaborative signals through controlled model-size scaling and prompt-noise robustness tests (Figure 2 and Table 2). Conversely, v1's shuffled-representation control testing the feature-encoding explanation is removed (Appendix B.3, Table 6). Existing component ablations, embedding visualizations, training-data analyses, and intention case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same significance statements and markings in the main comparison tables. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars; v2's added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds scaling and noise findings and LLMRank comparison results; Table 8 reports MovieLens-1M NDCG@1 of 0.3919 for AlphaRec versus 0.2485 for LLMRank under sampled ranking. The shuffled-control results disappear. Retained main-table raw scores are unchanged, but Table 3 fails to reorder its improvement percentages with the datasets, incorrectly assigning Movies & TV Recall improvement 6.79% instead of v1's 9.12%.

T1.justification: Equation (1) substantively revises the mathematical definition of the initial user representation by exchanging averaging and nonlinear projection. This exceeds a notation change. No theorem, proof, formal guarantee, or new derivation is added.

C1.justification: v2 removes explicit new-paradigm and first-to-outperform novelty claims, qualifies the homomorphism conclusion as a possibility, and adds introductory claims about scaling and prompt robustness. The central claims of effective language-based recommendation, zero-shot transfer, and intention awareness remain.

C2.justification: v2's limitations explicitly acknowledge the absence of a theoretical guarantee, replacing v1's unresolved online-deployment limitation; the broader-impact discussion of attacked representations is also removed. The explanation for KAR/RLMRec trailing AlphaRec changes from language representations providing most of their benefit to their supposedly naive fusion design.

D1.justification: v2 supplies construction details for its new tests, including the random-letter perturbation and 19-negative candidate sets. Existing embedding extraction, model dimensions, hardware, optimizer, hyperparameter grids, query generation, and code access information are retained. Steam processing and the LLMRank model configuration are not adequately specified.

R1.justification: v2 situates AlphaRec within existing LM-based representation generators and reduces v1's explicit novelty positioning. It adds relevant context such as Pazzani and Billsus on content-based recommendation and Harte et al. on language-model initialization. Appendix A's main research taxonomy remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces a separate Preliminary section and reorganizes the narrative around uncovering signals, building AlphaRec, and exploring representation potentials. Research questions and appendix organization are revised, alongside terminology and citation-style changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds the scaling figure and noise/LLMRank tables, removes the paradigm-comparison and shuffled-control tables, redraws Figure 1, swaps the convergence/ablation panels, and reorders dataset columns. Displays are extensively relocated within a different document template, although most existing experimental plots are reused.

improvement.justification: The added scaling/noise analyses and direct LLMRank comparison provide useful evidence beyond v1, while the explicit theoretical limitation better qualifies the homomorphism claim. The gain is limited by removal of the shuffled-representation control, newly misaligned Table 3 percentages, sparse Steam evaluation details, and the unexplained user-initialization revision.
